negotiation.request: explicit profile name plus exact major and minor version in the simulation-create extension chain
negotiation.support_query: physical-device execution-profile properties report supported versions separately from qualification records
negotiation.omitted_request: legacy schedule and existing PmStepInfo semantics; never select this profile implicitly
negotiation.step_rule: PmStepInfo.timestep must equal 1/60 within one binary32 ULP and substeps must equal 1; reject instead of reinterpret
negotiation.validation_rule: core runtime enforcement is mandatory with validation disabled; validation may add diagnostics only
negotiation.version_rule: major changes may change schedule or material meaning; minor changes may add optional observability but cannot relax v1.0 limits
negotiation.qualification_rule: execution support and physical qualification are distinct; an unqualified adapter must never be reported as qualified

clock_and_presentation.high_rate_policy: interpolate previous and current committed snapshots; never extrapolate or advance physics for presentation
clock_and_presentation.overload_policy: at most one tick per render callback; retain dt=1/60 and allow simulation to run slower than wall time
clock_and_presentation.sustained_30_hz_result: 30 physics ticks and 0.5 simulated seconds per wall-clock second
clock_and_presentation.stall_policy: discard accumulated presentation debt after a stall, reset or background transition; never repay a backlog
clock_and_presentation.reset_policy: previous and current snapshots become the reset state and interpolation alpha becomes zero

input_envelope.compliance_conversion: response = 1 / (1 + dimensionless_compliance_ratio); apply the same generalized-mass conversion to linear, angular and volume constraints
input_envelope.rule: all global and applicable domain bounds must hold; a larger absolute speed never overrides a normalized travel bound
input_envelope.teleport_rule: teleports are staged boundary mutations, not motion during a tick; the target state must satisfy overlap and correction limits

algebraic_iteration_budget.policy: the following counts are exact for v1.0, never data-dependent maxima; an iteration cannot advance time or republish the spatial epoch

quality_measurement.units: SI unless a metric is explicitly dimensionless
quality_measurement.characteristic_length: minimum relevant contact diameter, rest edge, support radius or grid-cell width named by the fixture
quality_measurement.relative_residual: norm(residual) / max(norm(applied exchange), 1e-6 in the metric's SI unit)
quality_measurement.threshold_change_rule: changing a fixture, range, metric or threshold requires a new profile version and invalidates affected candidate evidence

coupling_application_rule: each registered capability must satisfy both endpoint domain gates and every gate for each enabled advertised mode; no pair-specific or backend-specific tolerance overrides

boundary_semantics.births: stage bounded proposals, build once including them, then apply deterministic identity-priority admission; rejection and intentional underfill are observable and never trigger another build
boundary_semantics.removals: unconditional removals apply at the next tick boundary
boundary_semantics.phase_transfer: solve-discovered transfer is staged for the next boundary; source removal and destination admission are atomic, and capacity failure retains the source
boundary_semantics.coupling_order: all endpoints use one published epoch and commit once; operator splitting is allowed only within the coupling metrics
boundary_semantics.topology_changes: stage at a boundary, invalidate affected warm starts and interpolation generations, and publish at most one new epoch

failure_behavior.known_invalid_input: reject synchronously before recording or submission
failure_behavior.gpu_discovered_envelope_escape: invalidate the tick and report PM_ERROR_INVALID_STATE on completion or explicit wait
failure_behavior.capacity_or_candidate_overflow: invalidate the tick and report PM_ERROR_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED
failure_behavior.non_finite_state: invalidate the tick and report PM_ERROR_INVALID_STATE
failure_behavior.recovery: caller changes inputs or capacities and submits a later tick; recovery work is separately measured

measurement.physics_time: host monotonic critical path from physics encoding start through physics completion, including required waits but excluding rendering and presentation
measurement.samples: retain all successful measured ticks including stalls; any failed tick fails the run
measurement.instrumentation: asynchronous GPU phase timing where supported; unsupported GPU timing remains unavailable and is never replaced with CPU time

performance.count_rule: every listed live/object/capacity count is exact; a run with a lower count, simplified geometry, fewer active interactions or smaller capacity is a different workload and cannot pass this tier
performance.applicability_rule: a target runs every workload supported by its advertised capabilities; an unsupported workload remains missing/unsupported and never becomes a pass
performance.render_rule: installed Gallery qualification separately proves that rendering and input fit the reserved time; headless physics timing alone cannot qualify a 60 Hz client

intentional_tradeoffs: one 1/60 time advance replaces the legacy profile's multiple time substeps
bounded compliance, damping and correction may produce up to the stated stretch, volume, penetration and drift errors
one shared spatial epoch uses conservative candidates and may do false-positive narrow-phase work instead of rebuilding during a solve
fixed algebraic work may converge less accurately than legacy adaptive or high-iteration recovery
deterministic source admission may underfill because rejected earlier proposals still exclude later proposals
phase transfers and solve-discovered removals have one boundary of latency
overload slows simulation rather than advancing a larger timestep or running catch-up ticks
presentation interpolation adds at most one completed-tick of latency

legacy_separation.comparison_policy: report both profiles with their own hashes, schedules, tolerances and results; never weaken a legacy threshold to make v1.0 pass
